Looking at this question, I need to identify which mouse immunization model was used to demonstrate CD90 as a marker for germinal center-resident follicular helper CD4+ T cells (Tfh cells).

The NP-OVA (4-hydroxy-3-nitrophenylacetyl-ovalbumin) footpad immunization is a classic and widely used model in Tfh cell biology. This model is particularly well-suited for studying Tfh cells because it allows researchers to simultaneously track:
- OVA-specific CD4+ T cells (the Tfh cells)
- NP-specific B cells (the responding B cells in germinal centers)

This dual-antigen system makes it ideal for studying T-B interactions within germinal centers and identifying markers (like CD90/THY-1) that specifically identify GC-resident Tfh cells.

[ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
